protocol.hypothesis: Reducing PPO entropy coefficient from 0.01 to 0.001 may narrow the stochastic-training versus mean-action deployment gap, while preserving survival and command tracking. Test with original and pure-yaw-mixture samplers, holding failure cost at -200.

evaluation.note: Fixed commands, no observation noise, randomized training reset distribution. Same reset batches across policies/commands. First trial only.

screen.selection: A candidate must pass its paired screen and the same checks against baseline. Prefer entropy-only as the smaller change if both pass. Otherwise retain baseline. No post hoc diagnostic may override a failed screen.
screen.note: Local recipe screen, not statistical significance or hardware certification. RMSE gates use arithmetic means of nominal reports; in-place means left/right. Survival uses all six commands, which reuse reset states.

protocol.budget: Twelve new full-budget trainings: six fresh and six resumptions, 138240000 transitions. Reuse twelve control weights and 360 primary plus 24 sequence reports; no early stopping or checkpoint selection.
limitations: Three training seeds per fresh variant, and three previously selected weak continuation chains.

Reuse final control weights and identical-condition deterministic/sequence evaluations from the preceding study; audit baseline source byte identity and control source provenance. New learner changes only the entropy coefficient.
Both training lanes use two CPU threads; CUDA disabled. Shared-host timing is not a throughput comparison.

sequence_protocol.purpose: Supplemental continuous command transitions after fixed-command evaluation; does not override the primary screen.
sequence_protocol.note: Supplemental 120-second continuous command sequence; cannot override primary screen. Control reports reused from previous identical evaluator.

control_audit.note: Nominal-pose evaluation has no reset or observation randomization; changing its seed does not create a new trial. All previous fields except seed match exactly; termination causes are additive. These checks reuse already scheduled reports.

control_source_audit.note: Compared all 102 package Python files. Only evaluator/CLI and the behavior-preserving termination-reporting block differ; all training wrapper functions and 100 other files match byte-for-byte or AST as stated. No assertion of a full native dependency graph hash.

production_audit.production_changes: Action clipping diagnostics, shared action limit, removal of redundant second clipping; selected recipe only if prespecified screen passes.

action_protocol.purpose: Supplemental paired sampled-versus-mean action gap and clipping diagnosis; no optimizer steps, not acceptance criteria or a deployment recommendation. Only action sampling differs within a pair. Independent clipping accounting compares raw actions against the environment stored actions.
action_protocol.commands: same six fixed commands as primary protocol
action_protocol.budget: 288 reports (144 mean, 144 sample), 9216000 maximum simulation transitions, no training. Actual transitions may be smaller if all first trials end early. Mean outcomes must match primary evaluations exactly; old sampled controls must match previous study.

resume_action_protocol.purpose: Supplemental continuation diagnosis declared after two fresh seed pairs, before continuation training starts. Same matched mean/sample action protocol; checks whether historical large exploration noise adapts. Does not alter the primary screen.
resume_action_protocol.commands: same six fixed commands as primary protocol
resume_action_protocol.budget: 288 continuation reports, at most 9216000 simulation transitions, no training. Mean outcomes must match primary continuation evaluations exactly. These are additional to the fresh action diagnosis.

recording_protocol.purpose: Post hoc recording of the observed short nominal failure in continuation seed 1234, right-turn command. Paired baseline recording. Descriptive evidence only; not an independent validation trial or a primary selection criterion.
